close_reason: False alarm: the depth>=1 vpns collection IS the correct RFC 5280 §6.1.5(g)(iii) implementation. The depth-0 root is always anyPolicy, making all depth-1 nodes vpns. For deeper trees, the cascade deletion in lines 2112-2129 handles descendant cleanup. Restricting to leaf_depth broke 7 PKITS policy tests. Added documentation clarifying the correct behavior.
description: In validate_path §6.1.5(g)(iii), the vpns_indices collection at ~line 2068 collects ALL nodes in the tree whose parent is anyPolicy, regardless of depth. RFC 5280 §6.1.2(d) defines valid_policy_node_set as nodes at depth n (leaf depth). For a 3+ cert chain, intermediate nodes at depth < leaf_depth could be incorrectly deleted by step (iii)(2) if their valid_policy is not in initial_policy_set. The fix is to add a depth filter: && nd.depth == leaf_depth to the vpns_indices filter predicate. The bug is latent in current tests because all PKITS policy tests use 2-cert chains (CA+EE) where depth-1 IS leaf_depth.
title: §6.1.5(g) vpns not restricted to leaf depth
